 disease with superimposed pulmonary edema given that the findings are
 fluctuating over serial radiographs.  A superimposed infection would be less
 likely.  Overall, cardiac and mediastinal contours are likely stable given
 differences in patient positioning between studies.  No pneumothorax.

 edema, acute respiratory distress syndrome, or atelectasis and/or focal edema
 superimposed on background pneumonia, noting that many opacities appear
 asymmetric, focal and fairly unchanging.
 
 3. ET tube is approximately 9 cm above the carina.  Recommend advancement.
 
 4. Persistent bilateral hilar enlargement, although particularly prominent on
 the right; this is probably due to pulmonary congestion, lymphadenpathy or
 enlargement of pulmonary arteries, and a combination of these factors. 
 However, other etiologies such as a mass are not excluded, and if this
 appearance were to fail to resolve to baseline following acute illness, then
 chest CT might be appropriate in follow-up.
